tool.name: disassembler sieve
tool.description: thin near-duplicate haplotypes with a k-mer diversity sieve

param.name: input
param.label: Haplotypes to thin
param.help: For example the reconstructed haplotypes of many accessions, collapsed into one FASTA.

param.name: source
param.label: Minimum sequence length
param.help: Shorter sequences are rejected before sketching.

param.label: Promotion threshold (tau)
param.help: A sequence is kept only if its estimated novelty against what is already kept exceeds this. The default suits gene-scale cohorts; the sieve's own archive-scale default of 0.15 collapses a gene cohort to almost nothing.

param.label: MinHash sketch size
param.help: Novelty finer than 1/sketch size cannot be resolved.

tool.help:
@HELP_SUITE@
-----
What it does ************
Thins a large cohort of near-identical haplotypes before alignment and tree building, which scale quadratically with the number of sequences. Each sequence is sketched with MinHash and kept only if it is sufficiently novel compared with the sequences already kept, so the output preserves the cohort's lineage diversity with far fewer sequences.
This is a lineage-level reducer. It is meant for large cross-accession cohorts. It does not preserve intra-host variation; use the walker's VCF or SNV table outputs for that.
The sieve is `kmer-diversity-sieve <https://github.com/stevenweaver/kmer-diversity-sieve>`_. This tool runs it with defaults calibrated for single genes.
-----
Parameters **********
========================== =============== ========================================== **Parameter** **Default** **Description** -------------------------- --------------- ------------------------------------------ Minimum sequence length 95% of the Reconstructions are often a few bases reference CDS shorter than the reference, hence the 5% margin Promotion threshold (tau) 0.005 Lower keeps more sequences MinHash sketch size 256 Larger resolves finer differences ========================== =============== ==========================================
The tool fails if no sequence is kept. Lower the threshold or the minimum length in that case.
